gen-dafont-groovy-gf-chocolate-classical: Groovy bends its funky letters like a single length of wire, with a slit where the c nearly shuts. Chocolate Classical Sans sits below with a broad-nibbed pen stroke that never curls closed, so paragraphs keep moving without a snag.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-comme: Friendly and a bit funky, Groovy leaves its c almost shut. Comme answers underneath in smooth, open sans-serif letters whose lowercase fills most of the height, so a long paragraph slides along without any clogged curves.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-cossette-texte: Arms and legs of constant width give Groovy its wiry, bouncy look, and the c barely lets any light in. Cossette Texte is the opposite: wide-eyed e shapes and a prominent x-height make the sans-serif body feel generous.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-duru-sans: Groovy draws every stroke as one uninterrupted line, loose and playful, with the c nearly sealed. A heading around twice the body size would let Duru Sans carry the text, since its wide openings and dominant bodies keep a plain sans line easy to follow.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-fresca: That narrow slit where the c almost closes is the whole personality of Groovy, loose and funky. Fresca lets its counters breathe into the sans around them, so the two never crowd each other.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-funnel-sans: Funnel Sans reads crisp and level, its strokes holding one width from stem to curve and its e pried wide open. But Groovy loosens things up above it, tracked out and wiry, so the sans text feels even more orderly beside it.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-gafata: Groovy goes first, friendly and funky, with a c that almost seals itself shut. Gafata follows with a tall band of lowercase under short stalks, and a wide-eyed e keeps long stretches of sans text easy on the eye.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-geist: Geist reads as quiet solid blocks of words, with a level beat and no stray accents of weight. Yet Groovy is the one with swagger, a loosely tracked, wiry heading, while the sans-serif body simply keeps its wide openings clear and steady.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-georama: Wiry, bouncy and slightly mischievous, Groovy draws its stems and joins with no contrast at all. And Georama, a plain sans with c shapes like a bracelet pulled apart and barely rising capitals, lets a long page unfold without fuss.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-gidole: Gidole reads like neon tubing, every stroke consistent, terminals held apart like open scissor blades. Yet Groovy above it is a closed, wiry thing, so the sans-serif text feels all the more lit and spacious beneath it.
